MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 11, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on December 11, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 7, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way, and at the Lawai Beach Resort, 5017
Lawai Road, Poipu, Hawaii (Council Member Goodell’s teleconference location).

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell (arrived via teleconference from Kauai, Hawaii at 6:31 p.m.)
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CONSIDERATION OF ADDITION OF LATE ARISING AGENDA MATTERS

City Attorney Curley announced that two matters arose after the agenda was posted and that there
is a need for the Council to take immediate action. For the first topic, he said he will ask the Council
to convene in Closed Session to hear information that he received Saturday from counsel involved
in the California Voting Rights Act lawsuit pursuant to attorney’s fees.

Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to declare that a matter arose
subsequent to the posting of the agenda and that the Council needs to take immediate action in
Closed Session to receive information regarding the Voting Rights Act lawsuit and the
consideration of attorney’s fees.

City Council Minutes  1  December 11, 2018
 AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Goodell

City Attorney Curley announced that the second topic is for Council to consider entering into an
agreement with Fédération Internationale de Natation (FINA) and USA Diving regarding a world
class diving meet that is proposed to be held at the Marguerite Aquatics Complex in Mission Viejo.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to declare that
a matter arose subsequent to the posting of the agenda and that the Council needs to take immediate
action regarding an agreement with FINA and USA diving for a diving meet that is proposed to be
held in Mission Viejo.

AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Goodell

This item was considered under New Business.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with legal Counsel: Pending Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Goodell joined
the meeting via conference call at 6:31 p.m.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council added a Closed Session agenda item to deal
with some pending litigation matters but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

State of the City

Mayor Sachs presented his State of the City video address.

*Note: At 6:31 p.m., Council Member Goodell joined the meeting via teleconference from Kauai,
Hawaii.

City Council Minutes  2  December 11, 2018
 COUNCIL-RELATED CEREMONIAL ITEMS

1.  Official Results of the November 6, 2018, General Municipal Election

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 18-52 Reciting the Fact of the General Municipal Election Held On November
  6, 2018, Declaring the Result and Such Other Matters as Provided by Law.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

2.  Administration of Oaths of Office

  The Oath of Office was presented to Ed Sachs by his wife Leagh, to Wendy Bucknum by
  her husband Paul and to Greg Raths by his friend Tom Pollitt and wife Luci. City Clerk
  Karen Hamman presented Certificates of Election to Council Members Sachs, Bucknum
  and Raths.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jim Farris, M.V.: presented written information and commented on various problem areas and
conditions that he finds unsatisfactory in the City of Mission Viejo.

Atty McLellan, M.V.: speaking on behalf of United to End Homelessness, she discussed services
that are available to homeless individuals and she shared a handout on her organization’s public
information campaign.

Ryan Reza Farsai, Sheridan, Oregon: presented various concerns that he has with the federal, state
and local governments.

The following expressed their support for Greg Raths for Mayor in 2019: Mark Martinez, M.V.;
Christina Adams, Dove Canyon; Adrien Kalfus-Diaz, M.V.; Leigh Ann Rowe, Dana Point; Tanya
Brown, Dana Point; Jay Djavid, M.V.; John Rodriguez, M.V.; John Salamy, M.V.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  December 11, 2018
 3.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of November 27, 2018, as
  presented.

4.  Check Register Dated November 16, 2018 in the Amount of $706,241.41

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated November 23, 2018 in the amount of $1,668,874.63

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2018

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2018

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October
  2018

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for October 2018

  Received and filed.

10.  Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo for the Fiscal
  Year Ended June 30, 2018 and related reports

  Received and filed.

11.  Federal-Aid Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Grant: Citywide
  Countdown Pedestrian Signal Head Installation Project (CIP 18237)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

City Council Minutes  4  December 11, 2018
 12.  Olympiad Road/Felipe Road Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP
  18236)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

13.  Marty Russo Youth Athletic Park Accessible Ramp Improvements (CIP 19313)

  Adopted Resolution 18-53 Amending the Fiscal Year 2018/2019 Budget for Costs Related
  to Capital Improvement Project 19313.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS

  Late arising matter added to agenda at start of meeting

  City–USA Diving Contract and FINA–USA Diving–City Contract; transfer of all
  liability under “companion” City, USA Diving and FINA Contract; Approval of both
  contracts for request to host, for a three year annual term, an international level
  diving event commonly known as the FINA Grand Prix

  City Attorney Curley announced that the City was approached by USA Diving, Inc., the
  nation’s official diving sport federation, with a request to host, for a three year annual term,
  an international level diving event commonly known as the FINA Grand Prix. FINA timing
  requirements caused USA Diving to request the City enter into a hosting agreement,
  whereby FINA, USA Diving, and the City were allocated event-related responsibilities.
  Mr. Curley said that in order to allow the USA Diving organization and FINA to proceed,
  two agreements are presented for the Council’s consideration this evening.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve Implementation, Duty and Defense and Indemnity Agreement regarding “Hosting
  and Staging Agreement for an Annual Event of the FINA DIVING GRAND PRIX 2019-
  2021” and non-liability of the City of Mission Viejo, California (“Agreement”) – City of
  Mission Viejo, California (“City” or “the City”) and USA Diving, Inc. (“USA Diving”)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  December 11, 2018
 14.  Purchasing Policy and Procedure Manual

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to adopt
  Resolution 18-54 Adopting the City’s Purchasing Policy and Procedure Manual Effective
  December 11, 2018.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

15.  Computer Systems Replacement Project

  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services, presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1)
  authorize staff to issue a purchase order to Dell, Inc. in the amount not to exceed $413,110
  for purchase of replacement computer systems and enter into agreement for any related
  deployment services; (2) adopt Resolution 18-55 Authorizing Execution and Delivery of
  an Equipment Lease-Purchase Agreement and Approving Related Documents and Actions;
  and (3) adopt Resolution 18-56 Amending the Fiscal Year 2018-19 Budget for the
  Purchase of Computer Equipment and Related Lease Transactions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

16.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Bucknum announced that there has not been a recent SCAG meeting so
  she had nothing to report.

STAFF REPORTS

17.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update from Chief Capobianco

  Battalion Chief Covey announced that Engine 9 and Truck 9 assisted Orange County
  Sheriff’s Department personnel and City staff at the Heroes and Helpers event at the new
  Target store. OCFA also participated in Team Kids at Del Cerro Elementary School and
  he presented a short video on the program. Chief Covey announced that 9 candidates

City Council Minutes  6  December 11, 2018
   graduated and were promoted from Fire Captain Academy 25 and 16 candidates from
  Apparatus Engineer Academy 29, including three who will be stationed in Mission Viejo.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum thanked the City’s Commissioners for their tireless work and she said
she is looking forward to appointing very qualified people during the next Commission
appointment opportunity. She also thanked the Mission Viejo Elks Club, of which she is a member,
for their benevolent work and she expressed her gratitude for the lovely flowers they sent after her
mother passed away recently. Council Member Bucknum also thanked Mayor Sachs for leading
the Council this year and trying some new and innovative things. She stated that each Council
Member brings their own skillset to the table and she appreciated Mayor Sachs’ focus on the team
aspect in his State of the City video. Council Member Bucknum said that she is honored to continue
working on the Council and she looks forward to what will come.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell thanked Mayor Sachs and Mayor Pro Tem Raths for their wonderful
leadership this year. He also thanked City staff and said he appreciates all that they do. He echoed
Council Member Bucknum’s comments on the Council’s teamwork and noted that they have the
best interests of the community at heart. Council Member Goodell said great things are happening
in Mission Viejo right now, he is proud to be a part of it, and he looks forward to continuing to
serve alongside his colleagues.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the Hanukah celebration and lighting of the
Menorah with Rabi Marcus and the Chabad congregation. She also announced that she and Council
Member Bucknum attended a Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)
conference in Los Angeles which was the 9th annual Economic Summit. She said they received
some really good information and they will share it at the next meeting. Council Member Kelley
also commended Mayor Sachs for his great year as Mayor. She noted that the Community of
Character word for the month of December is caring and she referenced materials that are
distributed in all 25 Mission Viejo Schools and include recommendations for demonstrating the
character trait. In closing, Council Member Kelley wished residents a very Merry Christmas and
said she looks forward to the Council’s next meeting in January.

City Council Minutes  7  December 11, 2018
 Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths thanked his family and friends, including Tom Pollitt, members of the
Chamber of Commerce and the Rotary and Elks Clubs for coming out to support him tonight. He
also wished everyone a Merry Christmas.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs provided an update on the recent Economic Development Ad Hoc Committee
meeting and stated that they are making some great headway. He commended the City Attorney
for his leadership in maneuvering through some interesting waters as the City moves forward on
the civic core project. Mayor Sachs wished everyone a very Merry Christmas and happy New Year
and he noted that Mission Viejo celebrates the holidays like no other town.

CITY COUNCIL ORGANIZATION

19.  Election of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2019

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to appoint Greg
  Raths to serve as Mayor in 2019.

  The following expressed their support for Greg Raths to be Mayor: David Collins, M.V.
  and Jim Froling, M.V.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Sachs, to appoint Brian
  Goodell to serve as Mayor Pro Tem in 2019.

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:51 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, January 8, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 8, 2019

City Council Minutes  8  December 11, 2018
